heading: Is there a government final expense program? (74 seconds)
name: Is there a government final expense program?
description: There is no federal final expense insurance program for the general public; the ads describe private life insurance that you pay for. This short video covers which public benefits do exist and how to check an agent's license before you share your information.
transcript: Saw an ad for a government final expense program? Here is what is real. There is no federal final expense insurance program for the public. The ads describe private life insurance that you pay for. State-regulated means your state oversees insurers and agents. It does not mean the state runs or pays for the plan. Social Security has a lump-sum death payment. A spouse might get a one-time payment of $255. If there is no spouse, some children may be eligible. You must apply within 2 years of the death. If you pay for an eligible veteran's burial, VA burial allowances may help. They cover some burial and funeral costs. Check the agent's license. Ask for the name, the agency, and the NPN. Open the NAIC Insurance Departments page. Confirm the agent is licensed in your state. Fair questions for any caller, including us. Are you licensed in my state? Is this insurance I pay for? Can I have it in writing first? Want to talk it through? Schedule a time at honorbrook-insurance.com or call (301) 615-8289.
